PlayerCsvDAO

class PlayerCsvDAO[source]

Bases: DAO[Player]

DAO for Player entities, one CSV file per record.

Persists each player in its own CSV file named after its ID and sanitized name, and keeps all players in an in-memory cache loaded when the DAO is created.

Attributes:
csv_handlerCSVHandler

Utility for reading and writing CSV data.

playersdict[int, Player]

In-memory cache by ID.

file_mapdict[int, str]

CSV file path by ID.

int_propertieslist[str]

Names of the Player fields typed int.

bool_propertieslist[str]

Names of the Player fields typed bool.

Methods

insert(obj)

Persist a new player and return its ID.

update(obj)

Update an existing player, renaming its file if needed.

delete(obj_id)

Remove a player and its CSV file.

select(obj_id)

Return a player by ID from the cache.

list()

Return all cached players.

search_players(query=””)

Return the players whose ID or name contains query.

Notes

Files are named <id>_<sanitized name>_player.csv and stored in the player directory of PathConfig.

birth_date is read with datetime.fromisoformat; an empty value is kept as an empty string.

generate_next_id()[source]

Return the next available player ID.

Returns:
int

The highest cached ID plus 1, or 1 if the cache is empty.

write_with_lock(filepath, data, headers)[source]

Write rows to a CSV file while holding an exclusive lock.

Parameters:
filepathstr

Full path to the target CSV file.

datalist[dict]

Rows to write, one dictionary per row.

headerslist[str]

Ordered column names; a header row is written first.

Raises:
portalocker.exceptions.LockException

If the lock cannot be acquired within 10 seconds.

Notes

The user directories are created if needed. The file is opened by portalocker.Lock in mode "w" with Python’s defaults, so it uses the platform’s default encoding and newline translation, unlike CSVHandler.write_csv with a path (UTF-8 with BOM).

load_all_players()[source]

Load every player CSV file into the cache.

Notes

Reads each *_player.csv file of the player directory; empty or unreadable files are skipped. Only the first row is used. Integer fields that are not plain digits (including negative numbers) become 0, and boolean fields are True only for "true" (any case).
